changes.after: A component is a function that describes one part of the screen.

before: A React component is a function that describes part of the screen. React calls it while rendering. Start with one heading, not a whole application. In this course the runner renders App for you; you do not write an import or a mounting command.
Define Welcome to return an h1 reading Trail station, and have App use Welcome. The starter is the small application to edit; the examples above remain available for comparison.
after: A React component is a function that describes part of a screen. React uses that description to show it. In this course, the app starts the component named `App` for you.
A component name starts with a capital letter. An HTML tag, such as `<h1>`, starts with a lowercase letter. Change the text inside `Welcome` to change the heading. `App` can stay the same.
Make `Welcome` return an `<h1>` with the text `Trail station`. Have `App` return `<Welcome />`. The text appears on the page, not in the console.

before: Read the small example and explain its inputs and effects.
Complete the starter for this lesson.
Run the behavior checks, then predict a changed case.
after: Run the checks and read the heading on the screen.
